keyVerseText: And Jehiel, and Azaziah, and Nahath, and Asahel, and Jerimoth, and Jozabad, and Eliel, and Ismachiah, and Mahath, and Benaiah, were overseers under the hand of Cononiah and Shimei his brother, at the commandment of Hezekiah the king, and Azariah the ruler of the house of God. under: Heb. at the hand
rootMeaning: The root of יִסְמַכְיָהוּ (Yiçmakyâhûw) comes from the Hebrew verb סָמַךְ (çâmak), which conveys the idea of bearing up, sustaining, or supporting. Combined with the divine name יָהּ (Yah), this name literally means 'Yahweh will sustain' or 'Jehovah sustains.' This etymology enriches the common English gloss by emphasizing not just support or help, but a divine, ongoing upholding and establishment from God Himself.
usageInScripture: The name יִסְמַכְיָהוּ appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 2 Chronicles 31:13, where it is translated as 'Ismachiah.' This consistency in translation shows it is used as a proper name, identifying a Levite who served as an overseer during King Hezekiah's religious reforms. The singular occurrence and faithful transliteration highlight the personal and historical significance of this individual within the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: The meaning 'Jehovah sustains' reflects a profound theological truth that God is the ultimate supporter and upholder of His people, especially those who serve Him faithfully. Naming a Levite with this title underscores the reliance of God's servants on His sustaining power in their ministry and daily lives. For the Christian faith, this name points to the faithfulness of God to uphold His covenant people, a theme ultimately fulfilled in Christ, who sustains all things by His power. It reminds believers that their strength and endurance come not from themselves but from the sustaining hand of God.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Chronicles 31:13, Ismachiah is listed among the Levites appointed as overseers during King Hezekiah's revival. The inclusion of his name, meaning 'Jehovah sustains,' highlights the divine support behind this spiritual leadership. The verse emphasizes the organized, God-ordained restoration of worship, and Ismachiah's name serves as a reminder that such revival and faithful service are upheld by God's sustaining grace.
